offence_severity: Death (Section 302) - Minimum: Life imprisonment, Maximum: Death
physical_harm: Wife of PW-5 died on the spot; PW-6 and PW-7 got injured
number_of_offences: Multiple offences charged, but only Section 302 was finally upheld for accused No.1
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the contradiction in the prosecution's case regarding who fired the gunshots and the lack of convincing evidence regarding the recovery of weapons from the accused.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the credibility of the main witnesses as questionable, noting contradictions in their statements regarding who fired the gunshots.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 23.11.1997; Trial judgment: 15.11.2000; High Court decision: 05.03.2009; Supreme Court decision: May 02, 2019
legal_representation: Ms. Jesal Wahi, Ms. Hemantika Wahi, Kabir Hathi, Advs. for the Appellant; Anuj Bhandari, Abhinav Srivastava, Ms. Ruchi Kohli, Advs. for the Respondent
investigation_status: Charge sheet filed against the appellant and other co-accused under various sections of IPC and other acts
appeal_history: Trial court: Convicted accused No.1 and 2 under s.302 r/w s.34; High Court: Acquitted accused No.2 due to doubtful identification; Supreme Court: Dismissed the appeal, upheld High Court's acquittal of accused No.2
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that on 23.11.1997, accused No.1 and 2 fired three gun shots which hit deceased Somiben, wife of PW-5, and injured PW-6 and PW-7, leading to Somiben's death. The FIR was registered against all accused under Sections 302, 307, 120B IPC read with Section 34 IPC and other offences.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the identification of accused No.2 was doubtful, and the High Court acquitted him by holding that his identity became suspicious, thus entitling him to the benefit of doubt.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that in the absence of definite evidence as to whether the fatal gunshot wounds were caused by a rifle or a double barrel gun, the judgment of acquittal cannot be said to suffer from perversity warranting interference.
